To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of people with intellectual disability are not accessing primary healthcare services; (2) the majority of primary healthcare professionals are not adequately trained to provide care for this population; (3) there is an urgent need to develop a research agenda for supporting primary healthcare professionals to provide quality care for people with an intellectual disability.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to demonstrate that people with intellectual disabilities have poorer health outcomes than the general population and that they are less likely to access primary care services.

the research agenda for intellectual disability is not only to improve the quality of life for people with ID but also to reduce the burden of disease and disability for people with ID and to increase their participation and contribution in society.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to support primary healthcare professionals to better care for people with an intellectual disability.

the primary care workforce needs more training in the care of people with intellectual disability, and that people with intellectual disability and their carers want this training to be provided by people with intellectual disabilities themselves, in a way that recognises the strengths and abilities of people with intellectual disabilities.
